searchText: That sentiment seems to be the consensus. I think the general thinking is that we have this giant state database, why not use it instead of the header when we want to add new things. Essentially, we shouldn't use the header for state data "just because we always have", we should use the header when it makes sense to be in the header for some reason. One potential reason is because block header data has different availability guarantees compared to state, and it is accessible in different ways.
